note: Adapted from Silvestri's 1914 original description (in Latin), original name Mimeutermes Giffardii sp. n. (spelled M. giffardi in Snyder's 1949 catalogue); covers the alate (♀), nymph, soldier and worker castes with measurements; type locality Camayenne, French Guinea, additional locality Aburi, Gold Coast. The original measurements use a comma as the decimal separator (0,78 etc.), transcribed here as 0.78 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate head black to chestnut, thorax chestnut, abdominal dorsum pale chestnut and venter pinkish chestnut, the middle part pale ochre-yellow; antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 about 1/3 longer than segment 2 and with an indistinct, incomplete dividing line. Soldier head snaky in colour, nasus brick-red to chestnut-red, antennae 12-segmented, segment 3 slightly shorter than segment 2 — the 12-segmented antenna is an important character separating it from M. sorex and other species of the genus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Alate (♀): head black to chestnut, thorax chestnut, abdominal dorsum pale chestnut, venter pinkish chestnut, the middle pale ochre-yellow; wings missing in this type specimen. Dorsal surface of head with many short hairs and densely clustered punctures, and with a few rather long hairs. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 about 1/3 longer than segment 2, with an indistinct, incomplete dividing line; segment 4 nearly as long as segment 2 and slightly shorter than segment 5; in another specimen one antenna 14-segmented and the other 15-segmented, segment 3 narrower and shorter than segment 2, segment 4 about twice as long as segment 3 and slightly longer than segment 5; the specimen from Aburi has 15-segmented antennae, segment 3 shorter than both segments 2 and 4. Thoracic nota and legs as figured. Abdominal tergites with short hairs, sternites also with a few rather long hairs. Measurements: body length 5 mm; head length 0.78 mm; head width 0.71 mm; longitudinal diameter of eye 0.52 mm; antennal length 1.5 mm; hind tibia length 0.85 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier: body straw-yellow, head ochre-brown to rusty, or brick-brown to rusty, nasus brick-red to chestnut-red, abdomen greyish from the intestinal contents. Head about 1/5 longer than wide, nasus gradually narrowing and slightly longer than the rest of the head, its surface with very fine linear granulation and a few minute hairs, plus 3+3 short hairs; antennae 12-segmented, segment 3 slightly shorter than segment 2, segment 4 nearly as long as segment 2 and only slightly shorter than segment 5. Anterior lobe of pronotum slightly concave in the middle of the anterior margin. Fore tibia with rather short hairs beneath, outer spines indistinct or absent; mid tibia with 2 or a few spines (or spine-like hairs) on the outer side; hind tibia with rather many short, stout spine-like hairs at the apex and 2—4 outer spines. Abdominal tergites and sternites with very short but rather numerous hairs and a few shorter apical hairs. Measurements: body length 3.5 mm; head length 1.33 mm; head width 0.75 mm; nasus length 0.78 mm; antennal length 1.20 mm; hind tibia length 0.54 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Worker: body straw-yellow, head milk-white, abdomen greyish from the intestinal contents. Dorsal surface of head with very short hairs, rather short hairs and short hairs; antennae 13-segmented, segment 2 narrower than segment 3 and twice as long, segment 4 about 1.3 times as long as segment 3, segment 5 nearly as long as segment 4. Anterior lobe of pronotum slightly concave in the middle of the anterior margin. Abdominal hairs slightly longer than in the soldier. Measurements: body length 3.5 mm; head length 0.65 mm; head width 0.72 mm; antennal length 1.10 mm; hind tibia length 0.55 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Distribution and habits: Camayenne, French Guinea (type locality) and Aburi, Gold Coast; the Aburi specimens are slightly larger, with the soldier head brick-red and the nasus chestnut-red. The nest occurs in humus about 10 cm deep, consisting of small chambers and interconnecting galleries; in one case at Conakry its nest was mixed with those of Procubitermes acutifrons and Pericapritermes urgens var. confinis. Soldiers are numerous, about 1 per 20—30 workers.
